rule: On a 1/0 checkerboard ((r+c) even = 1), each diamond badge has a centre that stays 1 and an 8-cell ring at (±2,0), (0,±2), (±1,±1). Each diagonal side (sy,sx) may carry a 3-cell segment at centre + (sy*a, sx*(4-a)) for a=1..3. In the output, the two end cells (a=1, a=3) of each segment shoot a ray of the segment colour in direction (sy,sx) to the border, recolouring checker-1 cells. The middle cell shoots nothing. Off-grid end cells produce no visible ray.
scope: Checkerboard diamond badges emit diagonal rays from segment endpoints; 1..4 badges, supported7..30 sides, clipped outer segments, independent dimensions and repeated segment colours. Canonical phase and background/checker palette retained.

authored_scope: Supported: random grid sizes 12..30 (the lower bound is raised for 3 or 4 requested badges); explicit sizes 7..30. Non-fixture sizes are synthetic extensions. Random scenes have 1-4 badges and 1-4 segments per badge. Placement is border-biased on all four edges symmetrically, so cut-off badges with partially or fully off-grid segment ends occur. Corner-pointing, no-effect segments occur as a synthetic extension. Segment colours may repeat and may equal other badges' ring colours. Explicit latent `patterns` reconstruct all fixtures. Deliberately not supported: rays crossing rays or other badges (so occlusion/order is never decided); segment colour equal to its own ring colour; checker colours or phase other than 1/0 with (0,0)=1; a non-zero background.
authored_constraints: Badge centre is a checker-1 cell ((cy+cx) even) with the ring fully inside the grid
Badge diamonds (L1 radius 4) are pairwise disjoint: centre L1 distance >= 10
No ray cell lies in another badge's diamond or on another ray
Segment colour is in 2..9 and differs from its own badge's ring colour
Count of 0 > count of 1 > count of any other colour, so background and checker detection are unambiguous
The set of detected centres (checker cells with a uniform non-0/1 ring) equals the latent centre set
The input differs from the output (at least one visible ray)
num_patterns, if given, is an int in 1..4 and is honoured exactly or rejected with ValueError
